title: At the market
subtitle: Saturday morning with Maya — a, an and some
canDo: I can use a, an and some with food words.
I can buy food at a market.
teacherNotes: Sayılabilir / sayılamaz isimler bu derste başlıyor. En sık hatalar: "a bread", "breads", "rices". Ekmek, peynir, süt, pirinç, su: sayılamaz.
Türkçede "bir ekmek" doğal olduğu için Türk öğrenciler "a bread" der; a loaf of bread kalıbını verin.
Arap öğrenciler "خبز"ı "أخباز" gibi çoğul düşünüp "breads" diyebilir; İngilizcede sayılamayan isimler çoğul olmaz.
Rol yapma: pazar yeri. Bir öğrenci satıcı, diğerleri müşteri ("Do you have…? Some …, please.").

sections.title: Listen and read
sections.heading: The Saturday market
sections.scene: Saturday morning. Maya and Elif are at the market in the park.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Here we are — the Saturday market!

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Wow, there's a lot of fresh food. Look at those apples!

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I always buy some apples and a loaf of bread here.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: I need some eggs and some cheese for breakfast.

lines.speaker: seller
lines.text: Good morning! Fresh eggs, fresh cheese!

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Good morning. Do you have white cheese?

lines.speaker: seller
lines.text: Yes, we do. This is feta — from Greece.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Perfect! It's like Turkish cheese. Some feta and a dozen eggs, please.

lines.speaker: elif
lines.text: Ha! Of course. A Turkish breakfast needs olives!

support.tr: Tekrar oku. Doğru mu, yanlış mı?
support.ar: اقرأ مرة أخرى. صح أم خطأ؟

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: The market in the park
paragraphs: Every Saturday, there's a market in the park.
There are a lot of stalls.
At the fruit stall, there are apples, oranges and bananas.
At the bread stall, there's fresh bread, and there are cookies, too.
There's a cheese stall with cheese from Greece, France and Italy.
Maya buys some apples, a loaf of bread and some flowers for Rose.
The market opens at eight and closes at one.

sections.title: Grammar: a, an, some
rules: **Countable** nouns: you can count them — one apple, two apples. Use **a / an** or a number.
**Uncountable** nouns: bread, cheese, milk, rice, water, coffee. No **a / an**, no **-s**.
Use **some** with plurals and uncountable nouns: **some** eggs, **some** milk.
To count uncountable things: a **loaf** of bread, a **bottle** of water, a **cup** of coffee
examples: There's some milk in the fridge.

support.tr: İngilizcede bazı isimler sayılabilir (an apple, two apples), bazıları sayılamaz (bread, cheese, milk, rice, water). Sayılamayan isimlere a / an ya da -s gelmez: "a bread" veya "breads" denmez. Bunun yerine some bread (biraz ekmek) ya da a loaf of bread (bir somun ekmek) denir.
support.ar: في الإنجليزية أسماء معدودة (an apple, two apples) وأسماء غير معدودة (bread, cheese, milk, rice, water). لا نضع a / an ولا s مع غير المعدود: لا نقول «a bread» ولا «breads»، بل some bread (بعض الخبز) أو a loaf of bread (رغيف خبز). ونستخدم some مع الجمع ومع غير المعدود.

tr.note: Türkçede "bir ekmek" deriz, ama İngilizcede bread sayılamaz.

ar.note: لا تجمع الأسماء غير المعدودة مثل bread و rice و cheese.
right: I buy some bread and some cheese.
